title: Rigorous targeting of the tumour is not necessary

markdown.headingText: Rigorous targeting of the tumour is not necessary
markdown.markdown:
```{python}
#| include: false
from cohort_common import *
from tumours import sizes, imaging_sizes, cancer_breasts

usable_results = rule_results(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
found = rule_breasts(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)

# every CANCER breast with a size, split by whether it has a usable (water-rich) scan
usable_cancer = {key for key, (label, *_) in found.items() if label == "CANCER"}
def size_groups(size_of):
    """(usable sizes, rejected-only sizes) for CANCER breasts in size_of."""
    usable, rejected = [], []
    for key in sorted(cancer_breasts):
        if key not in size_of:
            continue
        (usable if key in usable_cancer else rejected).append(size_of[key])
    return np.array(usable), np.array(rejected)

biopsy_use, biopsy_rej = size_groups(sizes)
imaging_use, imaging_rej = size_groups(imaging_sizes)
biopsy_all = np.concatenate([biopsy_use, biopsy_rej]) if len(biopsy_rej) else biopsy_use
imaging_all = np.concatenate([imaging_use, imaging_rej]) if len(imaging_rej) else imaging_use
scans_per_cancer = [sum(1 for nn, ss, label, *_ in scan_records if nn == n and ss == s and label == "CANCER")
                    for n, s in cancer_breasts]
median_scans = int(np.median(scans_per_cancer)) if scans_per_cancer else 0
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding 3"}
**Rigorous targeting of the tumour is not necessary.** The tumours we have analysed are small —
`{python} f"{biopsy_all.min():.0f}–{biopsy_all.max():.0f}"` mm on biopsy
(`{python} len(biopsy_all)` breasts) and `{python} f"{imaging_all.min():.0f}–{imaging_all.max():.0f}"` mm on imaging
(`{python} len(imaging_all)` breasts) — and each breast is measured with only about `{python} median_scans` beams, placed approximately from the
mammogram or ultrasound. The chance that those beams hit the tumour itself is small. Yet where the beams go through glandular, water-rich tissue,
the CANCER breast has the higher Water:Fat in **`{python} rule_text(usable_results, "CANCER vs NORMAL")`** of patients (@sec-the-rule). The
data point to **wide-reaching changes in the breast, but in the glandular tissue**, not to a signal that needs the tumour in the beam.
:::

## The tumours are small; the beams are few

```{python}
#| label: fig-tumour-sizes
#| fig-cap: "Tumour size of every CANCER breast with a reported size. **Left**: linear extent in the biopsy cores (pathology). **Right**: largest mass on imaging (mammogram, ultrasound or MRI). Blue: breast has at least one usable, water-rich scan; grey: only rejected (fatty) scans. One dot per breast."
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, (biopsy_ax, imaging_ax) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.6), sharey=False)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

def plot_usable_rejected(ax, usable_vals, rejected_vals, ylabel, title):
    groups = [(0, usable_vals, TOP_COLOUR, "usable scan"), (1, rejected_vals, "grey", "rejected scans only")]
    box_with_points(ax, [(x, list(vals), colour) for x, vals, colour, _ in groups if len(vals)], rng)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1], [f"usable\n(n = {len(usable_vals)})", f"rejected only\n(n = {len(rejected_vals)})"])
    ax.set(ylabel=ylabel, title=title, ylim=(0, None))
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
    from matplotlib.patches import Patch
    ax.legend(handles=[Patch(color=TOP_COLOUR, alpha=0.5, label="usable (water-rich) scan"),
                       Patch(color="grey", alpha=0.5, label="rejected scans only")],
              frameon=False, loc="upper right", fontsize=6)

plot_usable_rejected(biopsy_ax, biopsy_use, biopsy_rej, "Linear extent (mm)", "Biopsy cores")
plot_usable_rejected(imaging_ax, imaging_use, imaging_rej, "Largest mass on imaging (mm)", "Imaging")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

Over every CANCER breast with a reported size, the tumours run from `{python} f"{biopsy_all.min():.0f}"` to
`{python} f"{biopsy_all.max():.0f}"` mm on biopsy (median `{python} f"{np.median(biopsy_all):.0f}"` mm,
`{python} len(biopsy_all)` breasts) and from `{python} f"{imaging_all.min():.0f}"` to
`{python} f"{imaging_all.max():.0f}"` mm on imaging (median `{python} f"{np.median(imaging_all):.0f}"` mm,
`{python} len(imaging_all)` breasts). Usable and rejected-only breasts have similar size ranges (imaging medians
`{python} f"{np.median(imaging_use):.0f}"` mm and `{python} f"{np.median(imaging_rej):.0f}"` mm), so having a water-rich scan is not simply a
matter of a larger tumour. The biopsy size is only the length of tumour along a needle core; imaging measures the mass itself and is the better
sense of how large a target the tumour is. Even so, most are a couple of centimetres or less. Size by grade is in @sec-tumour-details.

Each breast is scanned only a few times — typically `{python} median_scans` beams — and the operator places them from a quadrant, a clock
position and a distance from the nipple. The breast sits differently on our instrument than on the mammogram. Hitting a
`{python} f"{np.median(imaging_all):.0f}"` mm mass with `{python} median_scans` approximately placed beams is unlikely to be the rule; missing the
tumour altogether will often be the case. We have no data on where each beam landed relative to the tumour, so this is an argument from the sizes
and the scanning practice, not a measured miss rate.

## Yet the glandular signal holds

What we do measure is whether each beam went through **water-rich, glandular tissue** (@sec-water-rich, @sec-the-rule). When both breasts have at least one such
scan, the CANCER breast is the wetter one in most CANCER/NORMAL patients, across the size range of @fig-tumour-sizes. Fatty scans of the same
breasts do not carry the signal. So the result does not require the tumour in the beam; it requires glandular tissue.

A working **hypothesis** is that the cancer changes tissue beyond the tumour itself — a **sphere of influence** — and that those changes are
expressed in the glandular/fibrous tissue of the breast. Tumours remodel the fibrous stroma around them [[5]](#references), and X-ray scattering
has detected structural changes in and next to breast tumours [[6]](#references) [[7]](#references). How far that region reaches cannot be measured
from these data. What the data support is the practical claim: **high positioning accuracy on the tumour is not needed**; what matters is that each
scan reaches glandular tissue.
